hypothesis.statement: THE SCOPING SCREEN ITSELF IS THE NEXT LANE'S ITEM, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE CORPUS HAS BEEN USING. Both cheap screens are unusable: a raw-JSON ANCHOR scan finds 2 of the 60 (because attempts anchor as `function:<Name>` and almost never carry a `tu` field, so the unit is only reachable through the symbol->module link), and the substring scan the previous sweeps used finds 69 of which 67 are not anchored to a changed unit -- a 97% false-positive rate on this unit set, against the 9% the run-54 sweep measured on its own. The only sound screen is `gdlmem.py find --tu <unit>` intersected with the denial-carrying set, and it is CAPPED: five of the seven units returned exactly 25 records, the default limit, so 60 is a FLOOR. Ship `gdlmem.py find --tu <unit> --denials` (or an explicit unbounded limit) so an expiry sweep can be complete rather than truncated, and the sweep becomes a one-command operation instead of a scratch script every custodial round rewrites.
